```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE)
library(tidyverse)
library(Hmisc)
```

# Introduction

With what seems to ever increasing factors that are detrimental to general health, we as medical practitioners are always on the look out for causative factors, common to most patients that may hold the key to preventive treatment plans that can be developed.

![](234c66d1244f4936282b8ecc81cc6b2054153882-5000x3750.jpg)

This data set holds data of a variety of patients including some who have been diagnosed with Lung cancer, this data set contains variable related to personal life factors of each patient.

Using R language to run statistical test and plot factors to try to discover any causative factors from this data-set.

## Data Preparing

Install Packages to be used in the analysis Using Packages such as Tidyverse and Hmisc

Load and explore data set gotten from KAGGLE learn:[<https://www.kaggle.com/datasets/khwaishsaxena/lung-cancer-dataset>]

```{r, collapse=TRUE}
lung_c <- read.csv("C:/Users/USER/Documents/Git_Hub Data/Data/Lung Cancer/Lung_Cancer_Trends_Realistic.csv")
summary(lung_c)
```

# Variables

Grouping/marking this data set by certain variables allows us to look closer at possible underlying factors. For this data set we will be looking at three groupings; Gender, Infection status and longevity.

### Infected

This new column identifies patients with lung cancer (of any stage), allowing us to visualize the data in reference to if they are affected or not.

```{r,collapse=TRUE}
lung_c$infect_dummy <- lung_c$Lung_Cancer_Stage != "None"
head(lung_c)
```

#### Death Rate

```{r}
lung_DeathR <- sum(lung_c$Survival_Status == "Deceased") / length(lung_c$Survival_Status)
lung_DeathR
```

### Gender

Separated by Gender

```{r,collapse=TRUE}
male <- subset(lung_c, lung_c$Gender== 'Male')
female <- subset(lung_c, lung_c$Gender== 'Female')
head(male)
head(female)
```

#### Statistical Testing

T-test between gender

```{r, collapse=TRUE}
lung_c$infect_dummy <- as.integer(lung_c$infect_dummy)
t.test(male$infect_dummy, female$infect_dummy, conf.level = 0.95, alternative = "two.sided")
```

### Longevity

Those infected with lung cancer (of any stage) but have lived for over 10 years following diagnosis.

```{r, knitr::kable()}
longev <- subset(lung_c, (2025 - lung_c$Diagnosis_Year) >= 10  & lung_c$Survival_Status == "Alive" &  lung_c$infect_dummy == "TRUE" )
head(longev)

```

# Plots

Data visualization of variables to get a better visual understanding on details

### Gender Stats:

```{r  ,echo=FALSE, warning=FALSE, error=FALSE}
lung_c %>%
  ggplot(aes(Gender, fill= infect_dummy))+
  geom_bar()+
  labs(title = 'GENDER'  , y= 'COUNT' , x= 'GENDER')
```

```{r  , echo=FALSE, warning=FALSE, error=FALSE}
lung_c %>%
  ggplot(aes(Gender, fill= Occupation_Exposure))+
  geom_bar()+
  labs(title = 'GENDER-EXPOSURE'  , y= 'COUNT' , x= 'GENDER')
```

### Yearly Report

```{r  , echo=FALSE, warning=FALSE, error=FALSE}
lung_c %>%  filter(infect_dummy == 1) %>% 
  ggplot(aes(Diagnosis_Year))+
  geom_bar()+
  labs(title = 'INFECTION RATE OVER THE YEARS'  , y= 'COUNT' , x= 'YEAR')
```

### Survival

```{r  , echo=FALSE, warning=FALSE, error=FALSE}
lung_c %>% 
  ggplot(aes(Survival_Status, fill = infect_dummy))+
  geom_bar()+
  labs(title = 'SURVIVAL STATS'  , y= 'COUNT' , x= 'STATUS')
```

### Not Infected

```{r  , echo=FALSE, warning=FALSE, error=FALSE}
lung_c %>% filter(infect_dummy == 0) %>%
```

# Conclusion

This report shows a lot a factors associated with lung cancer however there seems to be little causative factors among them.
